headline.headline: WHEELER SNUBBED BY ALL-STARS, ANSWERS WITH 14 STRIKEOUTS
headline.deck: Phillies ace dominates Reds on the same day MLB left him off replacement list
headline.body:
PHILADELPHIA — Zack Wheeler did not need a spot on the All-Star roster to make his case Tuesday. Hours after Major League Baseball released a list of replacement selections that conspicuously omitted the Phillies right-hander, Wheeler walked to the mound in Philadelphia and fanned 14 batters, leading the Phillies past the Cincinnati Reds in a performance that left the selection committee with considerable explaining to do.

Wheeler's 14-strikeout effort was the kind of outing that renders arguments superfluous. The 35-year-old has been among the most dominant pitchers in the National League all season, and Tuesday's gem arrived at the most pointed possible moment. The Phillies offense provided just enough support, and Wheeler did the rest, retiring hitters with a combination of a riding fastball and a sharp slider that Cincinnati's lineup could not solve.

The snub has become one of the more talked-about roster decisions of the 2026 All-Star cycle. Wheeler, who finished second in NL Cy Young voting in 2025, has posted numbers this season that rival any starter in either league. Whether the slight motivates him further is a question the rest of the National League may not want answered.

secondary.headline: BREWERS SWEEP CARDINALS WITH BACK-TO-BACK BLOWOUTS IN ST. LOUIS
secondary.deck: Milwaukee wins 4-3 and 10-2 in doubleheader, outscoring Cardinals 14-5 on the day
secondary.body:
ST. LOUIS — The Milwaukee Brewers came to Busch Stadium and left with everything on the table, sweeping the St. Louis Cardinals in a doubleheader Tuesday by scores of 4-3 and 10-2. The twin bill was a tale of two very different ballgames, but the outcome was the same both times: Milwaukee walking away with the victory.

The opener was the tighter affair, with St. Louis jumping out to a 2-0 lead after the first inning before Milwaukee clawed back with two runs in the third. The Brewers added single runs in the sixth and seventh to pull ahead for good. The nightcap was never in doubt after the seventh inning, when Milwaukee erupted for seven runs to blow open a game that had been tied at one. Jacob Misiorowski hit Wetherholt with a pitch in the first game, while Gasser plunked Crooks in the second. The sweep tightens the race in the NL Central and hands the Cardinals a difficult evening to forget.

secondary.headline: TATUM REFLECTS ON BROWN DEPARTURE AS CELTICS ERA ENDS ABRUPTLY
secondary.deck: Boston star calls split 'tough,' credits former teammate after stunning sign-and-trade
secondary.body:
BOSTON — Jayson Tatum broke his public silence Tuesday on the departure of Jaylen Brown, describing the end of their partnership as an abrupt conclusion to what he called great years together. The two had been the cornerstone of Boston's back-to-back championship runs, making Tatum's measured words carry the weight of something genuinely finished rather than merely paused.

The comments came as the NBA's conference semifinals continue and the Celtics attempt to move forward without the player who flanked Tatum for the better part of a decade. Brown was moved in a six-team sign-and-trade that also brought Khris Middleton back to Washington for a three-year, $17.6 million deal. Tatum said he was proud of what the two built together but offered no bitterness, only the particular quiet of a championship partnership that ended without a proper goodbye.

secondary.headline: ALFREDSSON LEAVES SENATORS LEGACY BEHIND TO JOIN MAPLE LEAFS BENCH
secondary.deck: Ottawa icon takes associate coach role in Toronto, stunning fans on both sides of the rivalry
secondary.body:
TORONTO — Daniel Alfredsson spent 18 seasons in an Ottawa Senators sweater, became the franchise's all-time leading scorer, and had his No. 11 raised to the rafters at Canadian Tire Centre. On Tuesday, he took a job with the Toronto Maple Leafs. The move, announced by Toronto as the NHL's second playoff round continues, landed like a thunderclap across Ontario and left Senators supporters searching for words.

Alfredsson will serve as an associate coach on the Leafs' staff, bringing credibility and experience to a franchise that has spent years rebuilding its reputation in the playoffs. For Ottawa, the hire stings beyond the usual competitive rivalry. Alfredsson is not merely a former Senator; he is the Senator, the defining figure of a golden era that ended with no championship to show for it. Whether he can help Toronto finally end its own championship drought remains to be seen, but the symbolism of the signing is unavoidable.

column.headline: BASEBALL'S ALL-STAR SELECTORS OWE ZACK WHEELER AN APOLOGY
column.body:
There is something almost poetic about the way Zack Wheeler responded to being left off yet another All-Star list Tuesday. He did not complain to reporters. He did not post anything. He went to the ballpark, shook off the insult, and struck out 14 batters against a big-league lineup while the same committee that overlooked him was busy patting itself on the back. That is either supreme professionalism or supreme contempt, and either way it makes the selectors look small.

The All-Star process has always had its blind spots, but Wheeler's case has become a reliable annual embarrassment. The man pitches in a major market, leads the league in multiple categories, and still gets passed over while names with shinier reputations collect the invitations. Tuesday night was his answer, delivered at 95 miles per hour with a slider breaking out of the zone. The committee should watch the tape, take notes, and do better next July. Wheeler clearly does not need the validation. But the sport does.

story.headline: O'HEARN SLUGS THREE HOMERS, 10 RBIs TO SET PIRATES FRANCHISE RECORD IN 12-4 ROUT OF BRAVES
story.deck: Pittsburgh first baseman rewrites history books as Skenes dominates Atlanta at PNC Park
story.body:
PITTSBURGH — Ryan O'Hearn delivered one of the most remarkable individual performances in Pittsburgh Pirates history Tuesday night, clubbing three home runs and driving in a franchise-record 10 runs as the Pirates hammered the Atlanta Braves 12-4 at PNC Park. O'Hearn, whose 16th homer of the season was among his three, carried Pittsburgh almost single-handedly through a game that was effectively over by the third inning, when the Pirates had already built a 7-2 lead with four runs in the first and three more in the third.

Pittsburgh starter Paul Skenes, shaking off a recent rough stretch, held Atlanta to just four runs over his outing as the Braves managed only modest contributions from Matt Olson and Eduardo Dubón, each doubling. Atlanta scratched across a pair of consolation runs in the ninth but never threatened seriously after surrendering that seven-run hole through three innings. The Braves, who entered the night at 52-38 and atop the NL East, had no answer for a Pirates offense that stranded 27 runners yet still pounded out 12 runs.

In a separate story reshaping the NL Central, the Milwaukee Brewers swept a doubleheader from the St. Louis Cardinals at Busch Stadium. Robert Gasser pitched a career-high 7 2/3 innings in the nightcap, a 10-2 Milwaukee victory capped by a seven-run seventh inning, with Joey Ortiz homering and Nelson Velázquez adding a blast as well. In the opener, the Brewers rallied from a 3-0 deficit, with David Hamilton and Brice Turang each driving in two runs during a four-run seventh inning to seal a 4-3 win.

story.headline: GRIZZLIES SNAG POST AS WARRIORS BALK AT PRICE TAG
story.deck: Golden State passes on matching $30 million offer sheet, sending reserve center to Memphis.
story.body:
The Memphis Grizzlies added frontcourt depth Tuesday when the Golden State Warriors declined to match a three-year, $30 million offer sheet for reserve center Quinten Post, league sources confirmed. The Warriors had until midnight to retain the 7-foot Dutchman, but chose to let him walk rather than commit $10 million annually to a player who logged limited minutes behind Kevon Looney and Trayce Jackson-Davis last season. Post, 24, averaged 6.2 points and 3.8 rebounds in under 15 minutes per game during the 2025-26 regular season.

The move gives Memphis a developmental big with shooting range at a position of need, as the Grizzlies continue rebuilding around Ja Morant following his blockbuster trade to the Los Angeles Lakers earlier this offseason. Post shot 38 percent from three-point range last season, a skill set that fits the modern NBA and gives Memphis head coach Taylor Jenkins a versatile option off the bench. Front office sources described Post as a centerpiece of the team's effort to build depth while managing salary flexibility.

Elsewhere around the league Tuesday, Boston Celtics star Jayson Tatum addressed the departure of longtime running mate Jaylen Brown, calling the split a tough but necessary chapter. Meanwhile, veteran forward Khris Middleton agreed to return to the Washington Wizards on a three-year, $17.6 million deal via a six-team sign-and-trade, his second stint with the franchise. Cleveland Cavaliers guard Donovan Mitchell also agreed to a contract extension, locking him into Cleveland through the heart of his prime.

story.headline: ALFREDSSON CROSSES ENEMY LINES, JOINS MAPLE LEAFS STAFF AS ASSOCIATE COACH
story.deck: Ottawa icon stuns hockey world by signing on with Toronto's bench staff
story.body:
Daniel Alfredsson, the most beloved figure in Ottawa Senators history, is headed to Toronto. The Maple Leafs announced Tuesday that Alfredsson, the Swedish winger who spent 17 seasons with Ottawa and scored 426 goals in a Senators sweater, has joined their coaching staff as an associate coach, a move that sent shockwaves through the Canadian hockey corridor and left Senators fans reeling in the summer heat.

The defection comes at a peculiar moment for the franchise Alfredsson once captained to the 2007 Stanley Cup Final. Ottawa announced Tuesday that 38-year-old star forward Claude Giroux has re-signed with the Senators, bringing back one of the team's most productive veterans for what could be his final productive seasons. Giroux, who torched the league for a career-high 35 goals during the 2022-23 campaign after arriving from Philadelphia, gives Ottawa a cornerstone even as the organization absorbs the emotional gut-punch of losing Alfredsson to its most bitter rival.

Around the rest of the league, the first wave of 2026 NHL free agency continued to reshape rosters at a dizzying pace, with analysts trading grades and hot takes over the flurry of contracts signed since June 30. Some deals have drawn widespread praise, others sharp skepticism, but no transaction has generated the raw, visceral reaction of Alfredsson's move to the blue and white. For a fanbase that once retired his No. 11 to the rafters of Canadian Tire Centre, the image of Alfredsson behind a Maple Leafs bench may take the entire season to process.

story.headline: QUARTERBACK CAROUSEL SPINNING FAST AS NFL TEAMS RESHAPE ROSTERS FOR 2026
story.deck: Several franchises are retooling at the most important position in football this spring.
story.body:
The NFL offseason has turned into a full-blown quarterback market, with teams scrambling to secure signal-callers ahead of mandatory minicamp deadlines. The Cleveland Browns, still searching for stability under center after years of turbulence, agreed to terms with veteran quarterback Sam Darnold on a two-year deal worth $58 million, banking on the 28-year-old's late-career renaissance to anchor a rebuilt offense. Meanwhile, the New Orleans Saints shipped their 2027 first-round pick to the Carolina Panthers in exchange for young starter Bryce Young, betting that a change of scenery and a stronger supporting cast can finally unlock the former top overall pick's potential.

The 2026 NFL Draft also reshaped the league's future, with the Tennessee Titans selecting Cam Ward out of Miami with the first overall pick after trading down fell through at the last moment. Ward, who threw for 4,313 yards and 39 touchdowns in his final college season, arrived in Nashville last week and immediately drew praise from head coach Brian Callahan during rookie orientation. General manager Ran Carthon called Ward the kind of competitor the franchise has been missing since the Steve McNair era.

On the free agency front, edge rusher Danielle Hunter agreed to a three-year contract with the Pittsburgh Steelers, giving defensive coordinator Teryl Austin a legitimate bookend pass rusher opposite T.J. Watt. The Steelers also quietly re-signed wide receiver George Pickens to a four-year extension, ending weeks of speculation that the explosive 24-year-old might demand a trade. With training camps set to open in late July, the offseason chess match is nearing its most critical phase.
